fitAnalysis.assessment:
This is a weak fit (28%) for a Go/Rust networking role that sits outside your current technical domain.

**Strengths:**
- 11 years of backend engineering, exceeding the 8-year requirement
- Kafka-based settlement service processing 40 million events daily
- PostgreSQL expertise and on-call ownership across 14 post-incident reviews

**Gaps:**
- Go and Rust are required primary languages; your stack is Kotlin, Java, Python
- No networking protocols experience (OSI L3/L4, TLS, Linux networking, CDN)
- ClickHouse, Grafana, and Kubernetes are missing from your toolset

**Recommendation:** Before applying to Cloudflare's egress team, spend time building Go projects and studying network fundamentals (TCP/IP, TLS, HTTP internals), then target backend infrastructure roles that bridge your distributed systems background with systems-level programming.

coverLetter:
Priya Raman
Toronto, Canada
priya.raman@example.com
+1 555 0176

October 12, 2026

Hiring Manager
Cloudflare

Dear Hiring Manager,

Distributed systems at production scale tend to surface the same class of problem: a service that looked fine under normal load starts degrading in ways that aren't obvious until you're deep in the traces. At Lumen Payments, I owned a settlement service processing tens of millions of events a day on Kafka, and when our payment status API began showing unacceptable tail latency, I traced the bottleneck to hot reads hitting PostgreSQL under load and rerouted them through Redis, bringing p99 latency down sharply. That kind of end-to-end ownership, from diagnosing the failure mode to shipping and monitoring the fix, is exactly what Cloudflare's "Run What You Build" model asks for.

Across eleven years as a backend engineer, I've designed event-driven systems, led architectural migrations from monoliths to distributed services, and carried on-call responsibility for a payments platform where uptime genuinely mattered. I wrote post-incident reviews that fed directly back into system design, which is close to the RFC and design culture the Egress team describes. My core languages are Kotlin, Java and Python rather than Go or Rust, and I want to be straightforward about that gap. What I bring is a strong foundation in building reliable, high-throughput backend systems, and a demonstrated pattern of picking up new tools when the problem demands it, including completing AWS Solutions Architect coursework during my career break to stay current.

I'd welcome the chance to talk through how my background maps to what the Egress team is building. I'm available for a conversation at any point that works for your schedule.

Kind regards,
Priya Raman

applicationEmail.subject: Application: Senior Software Engineer - Egress, Priya Raman
applicationEmail.body:
Hi Cloudflare team,

Your egress role calls for someone who can design and run production-critical distributed systems under pressure, and that's the work I've been doing for the past several years: at Lumen Payments I designed and operated a settlement service processing around 40 million events a day on Kafka, led a team of four through a nine-month migration from a monolith to six services, and owned on-call for the payments platform through 14 post-incident reviews. Go and Rust are not yet in my toolkit, but I bring 11 years of backend engineering in JVM languages and a track record of picking up new technologies quickly in production environments. My CV and cover letter are attached with more detail. I'm available to start conversations immediately and can interview any day from next week onward.

Best regards,
Priya Raman

followUpEmail.subject: Following Up: Senior Software Engineer - Egress, Priya Raman
followUpEmail.body:
Hi Cloudflare team,

I applied last week for the Senior Software Engineer, Egress role. Cloudflare's need for engineers who can coordinate complex production releases across teams caught my attention. One strength I didn't highlight: at Northgate Retail Systems I introduced contract tests that cut integration bugs found in staging by roughly a third, a discipline that directly supports safe, coordinated rollouts. I would welcome the chance to discuss how I could contribute.

Best regards,
Priya Raman
